correctness.rationale: With one priority per site, a possible influence at distance k requires a decreasing priority chain, so the infinite-line construction is well defined and is a factor of the iid inputs. With an inert ghost neighbor the no-B probability at the half-line boundary is 1−(1−p)∫f_B; the integral follows by conditioning on the boundary's only proposal, before which it is vacant. The swapped equation gives the stated hyperbolic solution. On (0,1] the boundary no-B probability is positive (its mark may be A) and strictly below one by the integral equation. For a marked all-A block with all proposals before t, every interior proposal succeeds automatically; only endpoint checks remain, against disjoint exterior inputs up to the two endpoint attempt times. This also works for m=2. The resulting product yields Eq. (1); the same single vacancy taken against two exteriors at one common time yields Eq. (2). Inclusion–exclusion for the two neighboring A events gives P_m−2P_{m+1}+P_{m+2}, including m=1. The intensities normalize over left endpoints, not occupied sites; the geometry and ratios remain valid at t=1 since pt<1. A/B symmetry and ergodicity give almost-sure ratio consistency for fixed lengths. Adjacent covariance is p²[(∫f_A)²−(∫f_A²)²]>0. The finite-chain DP and quadrature in verify.py were inspected, not executed; their frozen recorded checks are corroboration only. The exact replay is the half-line conditioning and inclusion–exclusion in RESULT.md §§1–5.
